source: IFRC Southern Africa: Cholera Appeal No. 03/2000, 10 February 2000 (via ReliefWeb)

source: IFRC Malawi Cholera Outbreak Operation Update #1, DREF/Emergency Appeal MDRMW017, 11 April 2023
processing_notes: Source states: 'Since the onset of the outbreak, Lilongwe has reported most of the cases (11,511 cases and 536 deaths), followed by Mangochi (8,369 cases and 123 deaths), Blantyre (7,699 cases and 205 deaths), Balaka (4,193 cases and 100 deaths), Salima (3,528 cases and 97), Machinga (2,303 cases and 86 deaths), Dedza (1,945 cases and 73), Nkhata Bay (1,517 cases and 44 deaths), Nkhotakota (1,438 cases and 58 deaths), Chiradzulu (1,361 cases and 43 deaths), Dowa (1,334 cases and 40 deaths), Ntcheu (1,247 cases and 50 deaths), Thyolo (1,153 cases and 32 deaths), Rumphi (1,049 cases and 17 deaths), Karonga (962 cases and 25 deaths) and Mulanje (845 cases and 31 deaths).' - interpreted as 11511 sCh cases, 536 deaths. Provincial subset - do not sum with national row. Cumulative since the onset of the 2022-23 epidemic to 17 March 2023, the as-of date the same report gives for its national figure: 'As of 17th March 2023, the cumulative confirmed cases and deaths reported since the onset of the outbreak is 54,324 and 1,671 respectively, with a Case Fatality Rate at 3.08%'. ARITHMETIC CHECK: the 16 named districts sum to 50,454 cases and 1,560 deaths, i.e. 93 percent of the 54,324 national cases and 93 percent of the 1,671 national deaths; the remaining 13 of 29 health districts account for the balance. Parts do not exceed the whole. TL is set to 2022-03-03, the Ministry of Health outbreak declaration date used throughout this dataset; this source places the index case one day earlier ('The first case was registered in Machinga district ... on 2nd March 2022. The Malawi Ministry of Health declared the cholera outbreak on 3rd March 2022'). Lilongwe: 11511 cases, 536 deaths.

processing_notes: Source states: 'Table 1 Summary of cholera cases and deaths by district [District | Number of cases | Number of deaths]: Mzimba 486/3; Ntchisi 68/2; Kasungu 90/6; Chitipa 91/3; Chikwawa 748/11; Mchinji 394/16; Phalombe 302/14; Zomba 759/28; Mwanza 120/5; Thyolo 1,520/36; Dowa 1,349/39; Mulanje 936/42; Karonga 1,403/25; Nsanje 607/21; Rumphi 932/18; Ntcheu 1,926/56; Neno 733/14; Mangochi 8,182/120; Dedza 2,124/95; Chiradzulu 1,426/41; Likoma 204/2; Machinga 2,708/104; Nkhotakota 1,461/56; Blantyre 8,975/190; Nkhata Bay 1,628/49; Balaka 4,111/81; Salima 3,591/97; Lilongwe 12,683/558' - interpreted as 12683 sCh cases, 558 deaths. Provincial subset - do not sum with national row. THE COMPLETE 28-DISTRICT TABLE for the 2022-23 epidemic, from the cleaned PHIM/Ministry of Health national cholera surveillance database (https://cholera.health.gov.mw/surveillance) as extracted by the authors on 20 May 2023; the paper's Figure 1 caption states 'Data were obtained from the Public Health Institute of Malawi (PHIM), Malawi Ministry of Health (MoH) data on May 20, 2023'. TL is set to 2022-03-03, the Ministry of Health outbreak declaration date used throughout this dataset; the paper's own figures span January 2022 to May 2023. ARITHMETIC CHECK AND ITS RESOLUTION: the 28 districts sum to 59,557 cases and 1,732 deaths. The same paper's national figures are 59,156 cases and 1,771 deaths (accessed 30 May 2024) and, for the CFR calculation, 1,759 of 58,730. District cases therefore EXCEED the stated national case total by 401 (0.7 percent) while district deaths fall 39 short. The two are not the same snapshot - the district table is a 20 May 2023 extract and the national totals a 30 May 2024 extract - and PHIM evidently cleaned the line list between them. Corroborating evidence that this table is a CLEANED dataset rather than a later cumulative one: Mangochi (8,479 at 12 April 2023 in the OCHA Flash Appeal, metadata index 97), Balaka (4,193 at 17 March 2023, index 95) and Rumphi (1,049 at 17 March 2023, index 95) are all LOWER here than in the real-time daily bulletins, while every other district is higher. The district table is kept as the authoritative final geographic attribution; the 2023 sitrep snapshots already in this file (Index 15-20, 175-193, 201-217) are kept as the within-epidemic trajectory. Each internal row is self-consistent: the printed incidence per 100,000 and CFR reproduce exactly from the cases, deaths and population given. Mzimba is reported here as a single district, not split into the Mzimba North and Mzimba South health districts that PHIM's weekly bulletins use. Lilongwe: 12683 cases, 558 deaths, population 2,626,901. Highest case count and highest death count of any district in the epidemic.

processing_notes: Source states: 'At the time of the mission Karonga had reported 196 cases with 3 deaths that occurred in the health facilities. CONFLICTING FIGURES WITHIN THE SAME ARTICLE: it states both '196 cases with 3 deaths that occurred in the health facilities' plus 'One death occurred in the community' (= 196/4) at the time of the WHO mission of 18-19 January 2018, and 'By then cumulatively Karonga had registered 193 cholera cases and 4 deaths'. CROSS-BORDER CONTEXT: the same WHO reporting links this outbreak to Kyela district in Tanzania, immediately across the Songwe river from Karonga, and notes a Karonga-Kyela cross-border meeting initiated in 2017.

processing_notes: Source states: 'Since the start of the 2025/26 Cholera season on 1 November 2025, Malawi has recorded a cumulative total of 3,013 local cholera cases, including 25 deaths (13 facility and 12 community). Of these, 319 were laboratory-confirmed cases, with 5 facility deaths, while 460 were epidemiologically linked cases. ... A total of 774 patients have recovered and were discharged. Based on the cumulative 3,013 cases and 13 facility deaths the case fatality ratio (CFR) is 0.43%.' - interpreted as 3013 sCh cases, 319 cCh confirmed cases, 25 deaths. National total - includes provinces not individually listed. Final cumulative for the 2025/26 cholera season. IMPORTANT REVISION: this bulletin restates the season death toll as 25 (13 facility + 12 community) where every earlier bulletin, including epi-week 33 published only ten days before, reported 5 deaths 'recorded between 9 January and 29 March 2026'. The 5 figure was facility deaths among laboratory-confirmed cases only; the 25 figure adds community deaths and suspected-case deaths. Rows carrying the old 5 (Index 57, 78, 93, 111 and others) are therefore not wrong, they use the narrower definition. The 0.43 percent CFR the bulletin prints is 13/3,013, i.e. facility deaths over all cases - a third definition again. deaths=25 is recorded here as the widest and latest count; CFR is computed as 25/3,013 = 0.83 percent. Cross-border cases are excluded from the 3,013, as PHIM states they are 'In addition to locally reported cases'.
